title: Taiwan Cement calls for anti-dumping investigation and carbon border adjustment mechanism
summary: Taiwan Cement calls for anti-dumping investigation and carbon border adjustment mechanism
body_markdown:
**Taiwan:** Taiwan Cement has asked the Taiwanese government to launch an anti-dumping investigation. Taiwan News has reported that the company said ‘low-priced’ imports account for 30% of the cement and clinker market in Taiwan. Imports are reportedly 10 – 15% cheaper than domestic product, while cement plants are operating at below 60% capacity. Meanwhile, Taiwan has no tariffs on cement or clinker and ‘relatively less stringent’ inspection procedures than countries like Japan and South Korea, according to Taiwan Cement general manager Cheng Yao-hui.


In order to protect the domestic industry, Cheng proposed new import rules like those used by Japan and South Korea, including stricter standards and certification requirements and favourable procurement. Taiwan Cement also pointed to a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) on the EU’s model as a potential preventative of carbon leakage amid on-going decarbonisation of the industry.


Taiwan’s government previously imposed anti-dumping duties on imports of Vietnamese cement in 2025, however Taiwan Cement alleges that the government of Vietnam lowered its export taxes in order to help absorb the costs. Taiwanese suppliers have reportedly lowered their quoted price of Vietnamese cement by a further 20% since then. Meanwhile, imports of Indonesian clinker into Taiwan grew by 50% year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026. Indonesian producers reportedly exported cement at 50% below their domestic market prices.
